name: arXiv monitor — fetch newest, judge relevance to agentruntime, whisper digest
description: Daily(ish) arXiv triage: a deterministic fetch node pulls the newest `count` papers from `categories` (default cs.AI) via scripts/arxiv-monitor.mjs, dedups against data/arxiv-seen.json (safe to run many times a day — arXiv only announces once per weekday, so extra runs are no-op), a judge agent reads the unseen abstracts against the actual repo and shortlists what could change how agentruntime is built, and the digest is whispered to `agent`. Fetch marks items seen immediately; if the judge node fails, the batch is preserved at data/arxiv-inbox/latest.json (it will NOT resurface on the next run). Params: count (papers to pull, default 30, cap 100), categories (comma-separated arXiv cats, default cs.AI), cwd (the agentruntime repo root — judge reads it, never writes), agent (who receives the digest). Preset 'arxiv-daily' has the standard values — prefer running that.

meta.description: Deterministic fetch + dedup. stdout is JSON: { fetched, new, items } or { error } — never ambiguous. Non-zero exit still flows downstream as ok:false; the judge prompt handles the error shape.

params.prompt:
You are the research-triage judge for the AgentRuntime project. Your working directory IS the agentruntime repo — read CLAUDE.md (and peek at packages/ or papers/ if needed) to ground yourself in what the project actually is: a container runtime for AI agents — multi-agent stigmergic coordination, MCP tool mesh, workflow DAGs of agent turns, session/memory/compaction management, multi-runtime dispatch (Claude/Grok/local models), agent training and distillation (residents), local GPU inference. Do NOT write or modify any files.

Below is a JSON batch of newly published arXiv papers (already deduplicated — you only see papers no prior run has judged).

=== FEED ===
{{nodes.fetch.result.stdout}}

If the JSON contains an `error` field, reply with exactly: FEED-ERROR: <the error> and stop.
If `new` is 0, reply with exactly: NO-NEW-ITEMS (fetched <fetched>, all previously seen) and stop.

Otherwise triage. Be strict: a paper is RELEVANT only if it could change how a specific part of agentruntime is built, or validate/refute one of its design choices. General AI novelty is not relevance.

Reply format:
RELEVANT (<n> of <new>):
For each relevant paper, one block:
- <TITLE> — <link>
  <1-2 sentences: what it contributes, and WHICH agentruntime subsystem it touches (name the package/dir).>
Order by relevance, strongest first.
End with: SKIPPED: <count> — <one clause on the dominant reason>.

meta.description: Judge — fresh Sonnet session, reads the repo for grounding, shortlists with subsystem mapping. Read-only by instruction.
Fire-and-forget digest back to the operator's conversation.
